docs.title: Welcome to letterboxdpy
docs.text: A modern, fast, and feature-rich Python library for scraping and interacting with Letterboxd data.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Core Letterboxd Entities: First-class models for User, Movie, Search, List, Watchlist, and Members.
  • WAF & Cloudflare Resilient: Built on curl_cffi using real browser TLS impersonation (chrome120) and RFC-compliant URL normalization.
  • Deep User Insights: Extract complete watchlists, chronological diary entries, user wrapped summaries, ratings, reviews, followers, and genre distribution.
  • Advanced Film Discovery: Discover films by genre, curated themes, release years, decades, or streaming services.
  • Trace-Locked Sessions: Authenticated account settings and profile updates via automated CSRF handling.
  • Deterministic & Typed: Strict type hints, comprehensive offline test suite, and clean snake_case JSON schemas.

docs.title: Development Guide
docs.text: This guide covers setting up your development environment, running tests, linting, building documentation, and contributing to letterboxdpy.

docs.title: Environment Setup
docs.text:
letterboxdpy requires Python 3.10 or higher.

Clone the repository and install all optional development dependencies:

git clone https://github.com/nmcassa/letterboxdpy.git
cd letterboxdpy

# Install in editable mode with development, docs, and example dependencies
pip install -e ".[dev,docs,examples]"

docs.title: Code Quality & Linting
docs.text:
This project uses Ruff for fast Python linting and formatting.

# Check for lint issues
ruff check .

# Automatically fix fixable issues
ruff check --fix .

# Format code
ruff format .

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: The test suite separates fast, deterministic offline unit tests from live external network tests against Letterboxd (marked as smoke).

docs.title: Run Offline Unit Tests (Default)
docs.text:
Executes parser and model tests in ~0.5 seconds without any external network calls:

python -m pytest

docs.title: Run Live Network Tests (Smoke Marker)
docs.text:
Executes integration tests directly against live Letterboxd endpoints:

python -m pytest -m smoke

docs.title: Run All Tests
docs.text:
python -m pytest -m "smoke or not smoke"

[!NOTE] Tests that require an authenticated Letterboxd session (e.g. test_auth.py) are automatically skipped if no valid .cookie file is present. This ensures the suite runs cleanly in CI environments without credentials.

mkdocs serve

docs.title: Strict Verification
docs.text:
To verify that all cross-references, docstrings, and navigation links build without warnings:

mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Pre-commit Hooks
docs.text:
Pre-commit hooks automatically check linting rules with Ruff and validate commit title length before each commit:

  • Ruff & Ruff-Format: Runs on commit to verify and auto-format staged files.
  • Commit Title Length: Validates that the first line of the commit message follows Conventional Commits and is at or under 62 characters (checked on commit-msg).
# Install hooks for both pre-commit and commit-msg stages
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type commit-msg

# Run manually against all files
pre-commit run --all-files

docs.title: CI / CD Pipeline
docs.text:
GitHub Actions automatically runs on every push and pull request against the main branch:

  1. Lint & Test: Validates formatting with Ruff and executes the pytest offline test suite across all supported Python versions (3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14).
  2. Verify Docs: Runs mkdocs build --strict to ensure zero broken links or documentation errors.
  3. Deploy Docs: Builds and deploys the site to GitHub Pages on every push to main.

docs.title: Examples and CLI Tools
docs.text:
The letterboxdpy repository includes a collection of production-ready CLI tools, data exporters, and visual analytics scripts located in the examples/ directory.

These scripts demonstrate real-world patterns for scraping, reporting, data visualization, and session management.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Examples rely on optional third-party packages for visualization (matplotlib, pillow), interactive reporting (Jinja2, rich), and spreadsheet creation (openpyxl).

Standard InstallEditable Development 
pip install "letterboxdpy[examples]"

pip install -e ".[examples]"

docs.title: Command-Line Conventions
docs.text:
• Run all commands from the repository root directory.
  • Arguments in <angle_brackets> represent user-supplied values.
  • Most username-driven scripts prompt for a username if omitted in the command.
  • Scripts supporting the --open flag automatically launch generated HTML reports in your default browser.
  • Authenticated scripts accept an optional --path parameter pointing to a cookies.json session file (defaults to ~/.letterboxdpy/cookies.json).

docs.title: Rating Distribution Plot (user_rating_plot.py)
docs.text:
Renders a Letterboxd-style histogram displaying the target user's ratings across all half-star increments (0.5 to 5.0 stars), along with mean rating and total rated film counts.

python examples/user_rating_plot.py bugracoskun
  • Output: Interactive Matplotlib graphic window displaying rating frequency and distribution curve.
  • Dependencies: matplotlib, numpy

python examples/user_plot_statistics.py bugracoskun

python examples/user_plot_statistics.py bugracoskun --start-year 2015 --end-year 2025

docs.title: Styled Excel Exporter (export_user_data_excel.py)
docs.text:
Exports complete user activity into an Excel workbook (.xlsx) featuring custom column formatting, header styles, and tabbed sheets for profile metadata, watched films, diary logs, and ratings.

python examples/export_user_data_excel.py bugracoskun --runtime --open
Flag Description --user <username> Alternative to positional username argument. --runtime Fetches runtime for each movie to calculate total hours watched. --force Overwrites existing exports without prompting. --open Automatically opens the generated .xlsx file upon completion.
  • Output File: examples/exports/users/<username>/<username>_data.xlsx
  • Dependencies: openpyxl, rich

docs.title: Comprehensive JSON Exporter (export_user_data.py)
docs.text:
Extracts every major dataset from a user profile into structured JSON files under an organized folder hierarchy.

python examples/export_user_data.py bugracoskun

Exports generated under examples/exports/users/<username>/:

  • user.json: Core profile details, follower counts, bio, website.
  • films.json: Complete catalog of watched films.
  • watchlist.json: Current watchlist entries.
  • diary.json: Chronological diary logs and review snippets.
  • lists.json: User-authored lists.
  • followers.json and following.json: Social graph entries.

  • examples/exports/users/<username>/watchlist_comparison.json
  • examples/exports/users/<username>/watchlist_comparison.html
  • Features: Computes overlap score, common films, and unique recommendations rendered via responsive HTML.

docs.title: Interactive Account Management
docs.text: [!NOTE] Account management tools require an active Letterboxd session. Generate a cookies.json using UserSession.login() or export browser cookies before running these scripts.

Configurable options include:

docs.title: Contributing New Examples
docs.text:
New utility scripts and reports are welcomed. Contributions should adhere to the standard module metadata header:

__title__ = "Tool Name"
__description__ = "Single sentence summary of what the script accomplishes."
__version__ = "0.1.0"
__author__ = "yourusername"
__author_url__ = "https://github.com/yourusername"
__created_at__ = "2026-10-29"

Guidelines for script contributions:

  1. Rely on letterboxdpy core models for all scraping operations.
  2. Put output files under examples/exports/.
  3. Provide descriptive CLI arguments using sys.argv or standard library argparse.
  4. Run ruff check and ruff format prior to submitting changes.

docs.text: This guide walks you through installing letterboxdpy and making your first queries.

docs.title: Requirements

• Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, or 3.14
  • Active internet connection (Letterboxd requests are sent over HTTPS)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install the package via pip:

pip install letterboxdpy

If you plan to run the included examples (which use matplotlib, rich, pillow, etc.):

pip install "letterboxdpy[examples]"

docs.title: Cloudflare & Network Resilience
docs.text:
Letterboxd is protected by Cloudflare WAF. letterboxdpy includes built-in safeguards to ensure reliable data retrieval:

  1. Browser Impersonation: Uses curl_cffi to mimic real browser TLS fingerprints (chrome120).
  2. Canonical URL Normalization: Automatically validates and appends canonical trailing slashes (/) per Letterboxd routing standards, preventing 403 challenge blocks and redundant redirects.
  3. Retry Strategy: Automatically retries transient network interruptions with progressive backoff timeouts.

docs.title: Authentication & Settings Guide
docs.text: The letterboxdpy.auth and letterboxdpy.account.settings modules enable secure authenticated interactions with Letterboxd for managing profile data, personal preferences, and private settings.

docs.title: Architecture & Security
docs.text:
UserSession is trace-locked: every behavior matches legitimate browser traffic with automated CSRF extraction and token management.

sequenceDiagram
    participant App as Application Code
    participant Session as UserSession
    participant Scraper as Global Scraper
    participant LB as Letterboxd Server

    App->>Session: UserSession.ensure()
    alt Session File Exists & Valid
        Session->>LB: Validate session cookie
        LB-->>Session: 200 OK (Authenticated)
    else Missing or Expired Session
        Session->>LB: GET /sign-in/ (Extract CSRF)
        LB-->>Session: Form + CSRF Token
        Session->>LB: POST /user/login.do
        LB-->>Session: Session Cookies
        Session->>Session: Persist to .cookie/session.json
    end
    Session->>Scraper: Synchronize cookies & CSRF
    App->>LB: Authenticated Requests

[!WARNING] Keep your .cookie/ directory private. Never commit session files to version control repositories. Ensure .cookie/ is listed in your .gitignore. On POSIX systems, letterboxdpy automatically enforces chmod 600.

docs.title: 1. Automatic Session Initialization (Recommended)
docs.text:
UserSession.ensure() checks for an existing session file. If absent or expired, it interactively prompts for credentials via the terminal:

from letterboxdpy.auth import UserSession

session = UserSession.ensure()
print(f"Authenticated as: @{session.username}")

docs.title: 2. Programmatic Login
docs.text:
For automated environments with environment variables:

import os
from letterboxdpy.auth import UserSession

username = os.environ["LETTERBOXD_USER"]
password = os.environ["LETTERBOXD_PASS"]

session = UserSession.login(username, password)

docs.title: 3. CLI Authentication
docs.text:
You can also authenticate directly from your command line before running scripts:

python -m letterboxdpy.auth --login

docs.title: Managing Profile & Settings
docs.text:
Once authenticated, use UserSettings to inspect or update account configurations:

from letterboxdpy.auth import UserSession
from letterboxdpy.account.settings import UserSettings

session = UserSession.ensure()
settings = UserSettings(session)

# 1. Fetch current profile data
profile = settings.get_profile()
print(f"Given Name: {profile.get('givenName')}")
print(f"Bio: {profile.get('bio')}")
print(f"Location: {profile.get('location')}")

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
Handle authentication exceptions cleanly:

from letterboxdpy.auth import UserSession
from letterboxdpy.core.exceptions import LoginFailedError, MissingCredentialsError

try:
    session = UserSession.login("invalid_user", "wrong_password")
except LoginFailedError as e:
    print(f"Login failed: {e}")
except MissingCredentialsError:
    print("Credentials were not supplied.")

docs.title: Films & Discovery Guide
docs.text: The films module provides discovery tools to explore movies on Letterboxd by release year, decade, genres, curated themes, upcoming releases, and streaming platforms.

docs.title: Generic Films Class
docs.text:
The Films class extracts movie lists from any valid Letterboxd catalog URL:

from letterboxdpy.films import Films

# Browse all-time popular movies (limited to top 5)
popular = Films("https://letterboxd.com/films/popular/", max=5)

print(f"Total returned: {len(popular)}")
for film_id, film in popular.movies.items():
    print(f"- [{film_id}] {film['name']} ({film.get('year')}) - Rating: {film.get('rating')}")

Common service slugs: netflix, criterion-channel, prime-video, hulu, disney-plus, apple-tv, hbo-max, peacock, mubi.

docs.title: Curated Themes & Nanogenres
docs.text:
Letterboxd provides deep thematic taxonomies:

from letterboxdpy.films import (
    get_movies_by_theme,
    get_movies_by_mini_theme,
    get_movies_by_nanogenre,
)

# Broad theme
epic_heroes = get_movies_by_theme("epic-heroes", max=5)

# Hyper-specific mini-theme

# Nanogenre
nanogenre_films = get_movies_by_nanogenre("post-apocalyptic-survival", max=5)

docs.title: Terminal Formatting Helper

Use print_movies to quickly inspect lists in formatted terminal columns:

from letterboxdpy.films import get_movies_by_year, print_movies

movies = get_movies_by_year(2024, max=5)
print_movies(movies, title="Top 2024 Movies")

docs.title: List Guide
docs.text: The List class allows extracting metadata, film entries, creation dates, tags, and notes from any user-curated Letterboxd list.

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
from letterboxdpy.list import List

# Initialize using list author username and list slug
film_list = List("bugracoskun", "cold-palettes-dark-cities")

print(f"Title: {film_list.title}")
print(f"Author: {film_list.author}")
print(f"Total Films: {film_list.count}")
print(f"Created: {film_list.date_created}")
print(f"Updated: {film_list.date_updated}")
print(f"Tags: {film_list.tags}")
print(f"Description: {film_list.description}")

docs.title: Accessing and Iterating Films
docs.text:
The .movies property uses lazy loading; film entries are fetched and parsed from Letterboxd only upon first access, and cached for subsequent calls:

# len() returns total films count
print(f"List size: {len(film_list)}")

# Iterate over movies dictionary
for movie_id, film in film_list.movies.items():
    print(f"- [{movie_id}] {film['name']} ({film['year']})")
    print(f"  URL: {film['url']}")

docs.text: Property Type Description list_id str Unique numeric identifier for the list on Letterboxd title str Human-readable title of the list author str Letterboxd username of the creator url str Canonical web URL of the list count int Total number of film entries date_created str ISO 8601 creation timestamp date_updated str ISO 8601 last modified timestamp description str Optional markdown/text notes attached to the list tags list[str] Custom user tags assigned to the list movies dict Dictionary mapping movie_id to movie dictionaries

docs.title: Members Guide
docs.text: The Members class extracts community member data, popular profiles, and leaderboards from Letterboxd.

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
By default, initializing Members() fetches the most popular members of the current year:

from letterboxdpy.members import Members

# Fetch top 5 popular members of the year
members = Members(max=5)

for index, username in enumerate(members.members, start=1):
    print(f"{index}. @{username} (https://letterboxd.com/{username})")
Example Members Output (members.members) 
[
  "schaffrillas",
  "kurstboy",
  "demiadejuyigbe",
  "zoerosebryant",
  "jaragon23"
]

docs.title: Custom Member Catalogs
docs.text:
You can pass custom Letterboxd member catalog URLs to scrape all-time popular profiles, monthly rankings, or headquarters staff:

# 1. All-time popular members
all_time = Members("https://letterboxd.com/members/popular/", max=10)

# 2. Popular this week
this_week = Members("https://letterboxd.com/members/popular/this/week/", max=10)

# 3. Letterboxd HQ staff members
hq_staff = Members("https://letterboxd.com/members/popular/hq/", max=10)

docs.title: Combining Members with User
docs.text:
Iterate through popular members to extract detailed stats for each profile:

from letterboxdpy.members import Members
from letterboxdpy.user import User

top_members = Members(max=3)

for username in top_members.members:
    profile = User(username)
    print(f"@{profile.username} - Watched: {profile.stats.get('films')} films | Followers: {profile.stats.get('followers')}")

docs.title: Movie Guide
docs.text: The Movie class fetches metadata, statistics, reviews, cast, crew, external IDs, and recommendations for films on Letterboxd.

docs.title: Initializing a Movie
docs.text:
You can initialize a Movie instance using a Letterboxd slug or external service identifier (TMDB ID or IMDb ID):

from letterboxdpy.movie import Movie

# 1. By slug
movie = Movie("v-for-vendetta")

# 2. By TMDB ID (integer or string)
movie_tmdb = Movie.from_tmdb(752)

# 3. By IMDb ID (string with 'tt' prefix)
movie_imdb = Movie.from_imdb("tt0434409")

docs.title: Search Guide
docs.text: The Search class provides full-text search capability across Letterboxd with support for category filters, result limits, pagination, and slug resolution.

docs.title: Basic Search
docs.text:
Search across all Letterboxd categories or restrict your query to a specific content type:

from letterboxdpy.search import Search, SearchFilter

# 1. Search across all categories
search = Search("Dune")
print(f"Total results on page 1: {len(search.results['results'])}")

# 2. Search exclusively for films
film_search = Search("Dune", search_filter=SearchFilter.FILMS)
results = film_search.get_results(5)

for item in results.get("results", []):
    print(f"- {item.get('name')} ({item.get('year')}) -> {item.get('url')}")

docs.title: Available Filters
docs.text:
The SearchFilter enum provides 12 distinct search categories:

Filter Enum Value Description SearchFilter.ALL "" Mixed results from all categories SearchFilter.FILMS "films" Films, movies, documentaries SearchFilter.REVIEWS "reviews" User-written reviews SearchFilter.LISTS "lists" User-curated lists SearchFilter.ORIGINAL_LISTS "original-lists" Original lists created on Letterboxd SearchFilter.STORIES "stories" Letterboxd editorial articles & stories SearchFilter.CAST_CREW "cast-crew" Actors, directors, and crew members SearchFilter.MEMBERS "members" Letterboxd user profiles SearchFilter.TAGS "tags" Member tags SearchFilter.ARTICLES "articles" Journal articles SearchFilter.EPISODES "episodes" Podcast episodes SearchFilter.FULL_TEXT "full-text" Full-text content index 
# Member search
member_search = Search("bugracoskun", search_filter=SearchFilter.MEMBERS)

# List search
list_search = Search("Cyberpunk", search_filter="lists")
Sample Search Response Payload (members Filter Mock) 
{
  "available": true,
  "query": "bugracoskun",
  "filter": "members",
  "end_page": 1,
  "count": 1,
  "results": [
    {
      "no": 1,
      "page": 1,
      "type": "member",
      "url": "https://letterboxd.com/bugracoskun/",
      "username": "bugracoskun",
      "display_name": "bugra",
      "badge": "patron",
      "avatar": {
        "exists": true,
        "upscaled": true,
        "url": "https://a.ltrbxd.com/resized/avatar/upload/sample_avatar.jpg"
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Pagination & Limits
docs.text:
Search provides methods to control how much data is fetched:

search = Search("Matrix", SearchFilter.FILMS)

# Fetch exact number of results (e.g. top 5)
top_5 = search.get_results(5)

# Fetch complete pages worth of results (e.g. 2 pages = 40 items)
two_pages = search.get_pages(2)

# Switch filters seamlessly without re-encoding query
cast_search = search.with_filter(SearchFilter.CAST_CREW)

docs.title: Resolving Film Slugs from Title
docs.text:
If you have a movie title string and need its canonical Letterboxd slug (for instance to initialize a Movie object), use get_film_slug_from_title:

from letterboxdpy.search import get_film_slug_from_title
from letterboxdpy.movie import Movie

slug = get_film_slug_from_title("Inception 2010")
print(f"Resolved Slug: {slug}")  # "inception"

if slug:
    movie = Movie(slug)
    print(f"{movie.title} - Rating: {movie.rating}")

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text:
The User class is the primary interface for fetching and analyzing Letterboxd user profiles, watched films, diary entries, social networks, likes, lists, and activity logs.

[!NOTE] Response payloads throughout this guide use sample mock data to demonstrate the returned schema structure without exposing personal accounts.

docs.title: Initializing a User
docs.text:
You can initialize a User instance using their Letterboxd username:

from letterboxdpy.user import User

user = User("bugracoskun")

# Basic Profile Data
print(f"Username: {user.username}")
print(f"Display Name: {user.display_name}")
print(f"Badge: {user.badge}")
print(f"Bio: {user.bio}")
print(f"Location: {user.location}")
print(f"Website: {user.website}")
print(f"Watchlist Length: {user.watchlist_length}")
print(f"Stats: {user.stats}")

# Get summary of all public lists created by user

docs.title: Reviews
docs.text:
Fetch all written reviews by the user across all films. Each review includes the movie info, log type, rating (parsed from Letterboxd's SVG star glyphs), review text, spoiler flag, and ISO 8601 date:

reviews_data = user.get_reviews()
print(f"Total reviews: {reviews_data['count']}")

for log_id, review in reviews_data["reviews"].items():
    movie = review["movie"]
    rating = review["rating"]  # float (0.5–5.0) or None if unrated
    print(f"{movie['name']} ({movie['release']}) — {rating}★")
    print(f"  {review['review']['content'][:80]}")

  "last_page": 4
}

[!NOTE] Ratings are parsed from Letterboxd's SVG star glyph elements (aria-label="★★★★½"). Both the current SVG format and the legacy rated-X class format are supported, so ratings are always populated when present.

docs.title: Activity
docs.text:
Fetch recent activity for the user or their followed accounts. Each entry includes a unique activity ID, ISO 8601 timestamp, a direct permalink (url), and a typed content payload:

# Own recent activity
activity = user.get_activity()
print(f"Total activities: {activity['metadata']['total_activities']}")

for act_id, entry in activity["activities"].items():
    print(f"[{entry['activity_type']}] {entry['date']}")
    print(f"  {entry['content'].get('description', '')}")
    print(f"  {entry['url']}")

# Activity feed from followed accounts
following_activity = user.get_activity_following()
Sample get_activity() Response Payload (Truncated) 
{
  "metadata": {
    "export_timestamp": "2024-10-29T18:00:00.000000Z",
    "source_url": "https://letterboxd.com/ajax/activity-pagination/bugracoskun/",
    "total_activities": 15
  },
  "activities": {
    "13321312465": {
      "activity_type": "review",
      "date": "2024-10-26T02:33:21.855000Z",
      "url": "https://letterboxd.com/bugracoskun/film/the-prestige/",
      "content": {
        "action": "watched",
        "description": "bugracoskun watched The Prestige",
        "movie": {
          "title": "The Prestige",
          "year": 2006,
          "slug": "the-prestige",
          "url": "https://letterboxd.com/film/the-prestige/"
        },
        "review": {
          "content": "One of Nolan's best.",
          "contains_spoilers": false
        }
      }
    },
    "13321312400": {
      "activity_type": "basic",
      "date": "2024-10-25T14:10:00.000000Z",
      "url": "https://letterboxd.com/film/inception/",
      "content": {
        "action": "watched",
        "description": "bugracoskun watched Inception",
        "movie": {
          "title": "Inception",
          "year": 2010,
          "slug": "inception",
          "url": "https://letterboxd.com/film/inception/"
        }
      }
    },
    "...": "..."
  }
}

[!NOTE] Activity types are review (watched + wrote a review), basic (watched without a review), and newlist (created a list). The url field is a direct permalink to the film page or list — useful for deep-linking directly to the relevant content.

docs.title: Watchlist Guide
docs.text: letterboxdpy provides two complementary approaches to access a user's watchlist: the dedicated lightweight Watchlist class, and the filtered UserWatchlist page handler.

docs.title: Standalone Watchlist Class
docs.text:
The simplest way to inspect a member's saved watchlist:

from letterboxdpy.watchlist import Watchlist

watchlist = Watchlist("bugracoskun")

print(f"Username: {watchlist.username}")
print(f"Total Films: {watchlist.count}")

# .movies is lazily evaluated on first access
for movie_id, film in list(watchlist.movies.items())[:5]:
    print(f"- {film['name']} ({film['year']}) -> {film['url']}")
Sample Watchlist Payload Structure (Mock Demonstration) 
{
  "username": "bugracoskun",
  "url": "https://letterboxd.com/bugracoskun/watchlist/",
  "count": 150,

docs.title: Advanced Filtered Watchlists
docs.text:
When you need to filter a user's watchlist by genre, decade, release year, or streaming provider, use the pages.watchlist handler on a User instance:

from letterboxdpy.user import User

user = User("bugracoskun")
Filter by GenreFilter by Decade / YearFilter by Streaming Service 
# Positive genre filter
mystery_watchlist = user.pages.watchlist.get_watchlist(
    filters={"genre": ["mystery"]}
)

# Exclude specific genres (e.g. no horror)
no_horror = user.pages.watchlist.get_watchlist(
    filters={"genre": ["-horror"]}
)

# 1990s films in watchlist
nineties = user.pages.watchlist.get_watchlist(
    filters={"decade": "1990s"}
)

# Released in 2024
films_2024 = user.pages.watchlist.get_watchlist(
    filters={"year": "2024"}
)

# Available on Criterion Channel or Netflix
streaming = user.pages.watchlist.get_watchlist(
    filters={"service": ["criterion-channel", "netflix"]}
)
Example Filtered Watchlist Output

  "count": 14,
  "data": {

      "year": 2005,
      "slug": "constantine",
      "url": "https://letterboxd.com/film/constantine/"
    }
  }
}
